title: Sagaponack / Sagg Pond
summary: Sagaponack is an eastern Southampton place-name also preserved in Sagg, Sagg Pond, and Sag Harbor. The name is connected with ground-nuts or Indian potatoes.
introduction_content: Sagaponack, also recorded as Sagabonock, is a tract in eastern Southampton. The shorter form Sagg survived in Sagg Pond, Sagg Harbor, and the modern village name Sagaponack.
history_content: The locality appears in Southampton records by 1651 and in many later spellings, including Sackaponock, Saggaponack, Sagabunnuck, Sagabonock, and Sagabonnac. Sachaponock is also treated as a mistaken form for Sagg Pond at Sagaponack.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a place where large ground-nuts or Indian potatoes grow, discussing the plant now often identified with Apios tuberosa.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place- and river-names have a remarkable longevity, often being used long after the local language has been forgotten or suppressed, and so they can provide indications of the form of early languages.”

— A. G. Brown, Documentary evidence and wetland perceptions (2009), Summary, 'Place- and river-name evidence'
preservation_content: Sagaponack shows how one Native place-name can remain visible across a pond, harbor, post-office name, and village name while still carrying older ecological knowledge about edible plants and local land use.
